trust_decision.summary: Bytes arriving on the engine-to-engine ZMQ PULL socket are peer-supplied and must not be decoded with pickle; the receive loop must use a non-executing codec and validate the message schema before the value is used. Decided in handle_zmq_recv at lmdeploy/pytorch/disagg/conn/engine_conn.py:79 (recv_pyobj -> pickle.loads), with the mirror decision on the send side at :74-75.

landing_point.why: The advisory names handle_zmq_recv in this file, and that loop's first statement is recv_pyobj(), i.e. pickle.loads on whatever the peer sent. The loop is started by p2p_connect (:65) on a PULL socket that connects to the address in the caller's request body (:61), and the distserve routes are registered without any auth dependency (lmdeploy/serve/openai/endpoints/distserve.py:39-41), so an HTTP caller can point the receiver at their own endpoint and feed it pickle bytes.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /distserve/p2p_connect (lmdeploy/serve/openai/endpoints/distserve.py:39-41) -> AsyncEngine.p2p_connect (lmdeploy/serve/core/async_engine.py:785-786) -> Engine.p2p_connect (lmdeploy/pytorch/engine/engine.py:498-499) -> EngineP2PConnection.p2p_connect (:60-66); also reached from proxy POST /distserve/connection_warmup (lmdeploy/serve/proxy/proxy.py:553-564) and by direct Engine.p2p_connect library calls
fix_sites.module_kind: library module, async ZMQ receive handler (no route of its own; driven by the FastAPI distserve router)

fix_sites.entry_point: engine migration loop after a KV migration: lmdeploy/pytorch/engine/engine_loop.py:558-559 -> EngineP2PConnection.zmq_send (this is the producer side that keeps the peer's recv path working; reached from the normal inference/serving path, not a dedicated route)
fix_sites.module_kind: library module, ZMQ send helper (wire-format producer)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The second pickle-over-ZMQ implementation (lmdeploy/pytorch/engine/mp_engine/zmq_rpc.py:121-126) binds tcp://localhost on a random port and carries an inline warning not to expose it, so a solver can argue it is a local, explicitly-unsafe parent/worker channel outside the disagg P2P path the advisory describes.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The legitimate cache-free notification a peer sends after a KV migration must still be produced in the wire format the new receiver decodes (engine_loop.py:558 -> zmq_send -> recv loop -> end_session). A receiver-only fix, or one that rejects every non-JSON/unknown message, silently drops the free: the migrated KV blocks are never released and a peer still on the old pickled format breaks. The fix therefore also has to change the sender, and must keep the 'invalid free' branch (session not in scheduler) as a log-and-continue, not a loop-killer.

O6_input_shapes: normal JSON object produced by model_dump()/send_json
malformed or non-JSON bytes (json decode error -> ValueError, skipped)
schema-invalid JSON object (missing remote_engine_id/remote_session_id or wrong type -> ValidationError, skipped)
non-object JSON values: list, string, number, null
legacy pickle bytes from a peer still on the old build
remote_session_id sent as a JSON string ('123'), which pydantic coerces to int

O8_uncovered_routes.route: AsyncRPCServer.call_and_response() pickles the ROUTER-socket request straight into the engine: request = pickle.loads(request_data) (and AsyncRPCClient unpickles server replies at :447/:451/:572); any local process that can reach the loopback port can execute code in the engine worker.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Binds only tcp://localhost:<random port> and is preceded by an explicit 'DO NOT allow visit rpc server from external network / unauthorized access may lead to code execution vulnerability' comment, so it reads as an intentionally-trusted local channel and a neighbouring feature of the disagg P2P path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package: lmdeploy/pytorch/engine/mp_engine vs landing point in lmdeploy/pytorch/disagg/conn; 1 file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second control message type handled in the same receive loop (e.g. a DistServeCancelRequest or a KV-block release request) decoded with recv_pyobj() in the same while loop.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The P2P channel already exists and is extensible; the repo keeps growing it (the 'invalid free' branch and the p2p_* endpoints are recent additions), so a maintainer adding a new peer message would naturally copy the neighbouring recv_pyobj line.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new pydantic control message added next to DistServeCacheFreeRequest and carried over the same pickled P2P socket.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: All distserve messages live in this one module and are already reused across the HTTP and ZMQ transports; adding a field/class here is the obvious extension point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shared-memory control path that pickle.loads whatever the writer process put in the shared buffer.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The mp executor already ships control/result objects through shared memory with pickle, so a new control message (abort, session free, cache flush) would be added on the same pattern.

O9_family: CWE-502 deserialization of untrusted data (pickle RCE over ZMQ)

O10_build.language: Python (plus optional C++/CUDA extensions for the turbomind backend)
O10_build.toolchain: setuptools + cmake_build_extension (pyproject.toml:1-5); runtime deps in requirements/common.txt (pyzmq:14, pydantic>2.0.0:13); the pytorch/disagg path is pure Python
O10_build.project_tests: tests/pytorch/engine/test_zmq_rpc.py exercises the mp-engine ZMQ RPC with a real subprocess; there is no test for the disagg P2P connection at the pinned commit (disagg appears in tests only as incidental imports of config/protocol/messages, e.g. tests/pytorch/engine/test_cache_engine.py:11-12)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Keep pickle on the wire and only tighten the isinstance() gate after recv_pyobj(), or harden the receiver alone while zmq_send keeps send_pyobj().

out_of_scope_notes: lmdeploy/pytorch/disagg/conn/engine_conn.py:44-46 binds the PUSH socket to a hostname taken from the distserve/p2p_initialize request body, and :61 connects the receiver to a caller-supplied address - a different mechanism from the pickle sink in this advisory; noted and not pursued.
unverified: Repository size in MB: no shell available, so not measured; the tree has ~1700 tracked files and is clearly far below 1.5 GB, and not obviously under 5 MB, so neither size red flag was raised.
Whether the O8 zmq_rpc pickle route is still present in the latest release: no release/network access available, so present_in_latest is unknown.
